newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Gunmen massacre 13, injure 8 in northwest Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen massacre 13, injure 8 in northwest Colombia.

text.p: Gunmen massacred 13 people and injured at least eight others in two attacks in trouble-torn Antioquia province in northwest Colombia on late Sunday, police said.

In a small town close to Turbo, in the notoriously violent banana-growing region of Uraba, suspected leftist rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) stormed into a tavern and murdered nine clients and wounded seven others, a police spokesman said.
Regional army commander Gen. Rito Alejo del Rio said a guerrilla column raided the town of about 9,000 inhabitants shortly before midnight.

"A group of FARC guerrillas threw a 25 pound (12 kg) bomb in the street but that failed to go off. They then began shooting indiscriminately at people from the tavern, killing eight instantly. Another died in hospital," he said.

The second incident occurred in San Pedro de los Milagros, just north of Medellin -- the capital of Antioquia province, where part of the Uraba region is also located. Unidentified gunmen killed four people and wounded one other, police said. A spokesman was unable to say who may have been behind the attack.
There was no immediate indication of the motive for either of the attacks nor of the identity of the dead.

It is the second mass murder in Uraba in less than a month. Just over two weeks ago a massive car bomb exploded in the town of Apartado, killing 11 people and injuring more than 50 others. The blast was blamed on the FARC.

For the past decade, guerrillas and right-wing paramilitaries have slain with impunity in Uraba. Some political analysts blame the violence on a conflict rooted in the struggle for control of lucrative drug and arms smuggling routes. Others, however, say the bloodletting surged after right-wing death squads and the military struck a covert pact in the mid-1980s to drive guerrillas and left-wing sympathisers out of the area.
